project.description:
Validates a psama.env against PSAMA's required-key rules and, only if it passes, uploads it to S3. The check is fail-closed: it requires every key PSAMA cannot start or authorize without, requires each identity provider's credentials whenever that provider's IS_ENABLED flag is true, and requires ENABLE_PUBLIC_ACCESS, TOS_ENABLED, CONSENT_BASED_AUTHORIZATION_ENABLED and APPLICATION_CLIENT_SECRET_IS_BASE_64 to read exactly true or false, because Spring also reads yes, on and 1 as true. An empty STRICT_AUTHORIZATION_APPLICATIONS is rejected as well: it makes no connection strict, and an empty merged access-rule set then grants rather than denies. Failures name the offending key only, never its value. An uploaded change takes effect only after redeploying PSAMA; the container bakes its env at create time. The rules are derived from PSAMA's own application.properties rather than from a live file, so run this job once per environment with VALIDATE_ONLY set against the current live psama.env before relying on the gate; that reports what the rules would reject without changing anything.
Before uploading, the job sets LOGGING_SERVICE_URL and LOGGING_API_KEY in the file from the shared configs/pic-sure-logging/logging.env that Render PIC-SURE Configuration writes, replacing any value already in the file, so PSAMA presents the same audit logging key as every other service. A missing or blank shared key refuses the upload. REFRESH_LOGGING_KEY re-uploads the psama.env already in S3 with the current key, which is how Rotate PIC-SURE Stack Secrets carries a new key to PSAMA. S3_BUCKET_NAME picks the bucket for both objects and defaults to the controller global stack_s3_bucket.

hudson.model.FileParameterDefinition.name: psama.env
hudson.model.FileParameterDefinition.description: Upload a psama.env file that has been configured and will be used to configure the pic-sure-auth-micro-app.

hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.name: VALIDATE_ONLY
hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.description: Run every validation rule and report the verdict without uploading. A file that fails still fails the build; this only suppresses the upload on success, so s3://.../configs/psama/psama.env is left untouched. Use it as a pre-flight: download the live psama.env, run it through here once per environment, and fix what it names before relying on the gate for a real upload.

hudson.model.StringParameterDefinition.name: S3_BUCKET_NAME
hudson.model.StringParameterDefinition.description: Bucket that holds configs/psama/psama.env and the shared configs/pic-sure-logging/logging.env. Every read and write in this job uses it. Leave the default to use the controller global stack_s3_bucket; Rotate PIC-SURE Stack Secrets passes its own bucket so the refresh lands where that rotation rendered.

hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.name: REFRESH_LOGGING_KEY
hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.description: Ignore any uploaded file. Download the psama.env already in S3, run the same validation, set the current shared LOGGING_API_KEY in it and upload it back. Rotate PIC-SURE Stack Secrets runs this after minting a new key. PSAMA must be redeployed afterwards.
